proved: The actual issuer creates and reads canonical credential records and creates Secret projections with an impersonated API identity; GET on both a database Secret and the projection is forbidden. Repeated issuance preserves the same credential.

Secret creation must match canonical record bytes. Record metadata changes and active DELETE/DeleteCollection are refused; removal and restoration of the webhook demonstrate the deletion guard. Retired records can be deleted.
Lost projection CREATE acknowledgment reuses the persisted canonical key, and issuance/Pod checks do not require Secret GET.

The runner authenticates the projected credential and live delivery authority over TLS before child execution. Invalid client trust, invalid server trust, revoked authority, and receiver unavailability prevent the fixture child from starting.
HEAD preflight publishes no records, rechecks authority on reused connections, refuses a body, shares saturation limits, and bounds a stalled authority check.
Lost result acknowledgment still redelivers identical bytes after one child execution, including execution-context cancellation.
The two rendered-chart tests skipped in the direct race command run successfully through e2e-static with both render inputs and the chart namespace/RBAC variants.
notProved: Manager receiver activation, publication-record admission, controller consumption, or installed durable delivery. The installed record webhook currently admits credential-role records only.
Installed webhook least-privilege permissions: real API tests use an administrator reader inside admission handlers, though the issuer itself uses the restricted identity.
Kubelet Secret mounting, real SQL mutation, garbage collection, trust rotation, backup/restore, manager failover, or full default-log maximum-plan workflow.
The supported Kubernetes/database/architecture matrix, production acceptance, and complete issue 586 DoDs. The 64 MiB workaround remains.
